column1: # Divider icon assignments. One row per section-divider slide, in deck order.
# `n` is the 1-based divider index within the deck, counting only section
# dividers -- the deck title slide is not one. Keying on the index rather than
# on the heading text keeps this stable when a section gets reworded, and
# tools/wire-section-art.py checks the recorded title against the file, so a
# drift is an error rather than a silently misplaced icon.
#   catalog  already in icons/ and unused elsewhere. Wired.
#   pilot    already wired on the C/07/a pilot, kept as-is.
#   new      one icon named in `lordicon`; export it and save it as `icon`.json.
#   choose   more than one candidate in `lordicon`, pipe-separated, because no
#            single icon in the library is clearly right. Look at them and pick.
# `state` is the Lordicon animation state to play. A raw file carries several:
# `in-reveal` starts blank and draws the icon in, which is what a section divider
# wants, and `default:hover-pinch` starts with the artwork already there. Icons
# with no states, which is every legacy file here, ignore the attribute and play
# their single animation, so `in-reveal` is safe to set on all of them.
# One row differs. `parabola` (square-root) renders a bare radical with NO accent
# in its default and in-reveal states; `morph-squared` is the state that both
# brings the accent back and draws the squared symbol the section is about.
# `lordicon` is the icon's NAME in the Wired / Outline family. That is what you
# search for, and the only field you need to find and export one:
# `key` is the icon's CDN code. It is provenance only: these decks use the `lif`
# shortcode, which reads a file out of icons/, so no code is ever fetched at
# render time. It is recorded because icon-map.json is keyed on it. An earlier
# version of this header claimed a code could be opened at
# lordicon.com/icon/<key>/wired/outline; that URL 404s and never worked.
# EXPORTING: set secondary to #2a76dd in the customizer BEFORE exporting, or the
# icon bakes in Lordicon's green with no way to recolour it at runtime. See
# ICONS.md, where that was learned the expensive way. Save into icons/ under the
# `icon` name, add the code to icon-map.json, then run
# Reserved and deliberately not reused: map.json, the roadmap slide's recurring
# motif across six decks, and the 25 other icons already carrying meaning on a

column9: note
The deck's own metaphor: computer as engine, RStudio as dashboard, package as add-on. Replaces browser-code, which said IDE but not this deck's IDE.
A prompt waiting for one line, not a whole editor.
Document with a pencil: a file you write and keep.

The self-contained project directory. Its in-reveal and default states draw a closed folder with no accent; hover-adding-files is the one that colours, and files going into a folder says Projects better than a shut one.
Source becoming a finished document. PROPOSED: parchment-writing (axmewqez).
Plain text acquiring structure. PROPOSED: inkwell (vzpsvgmn).
A book of name-to-number lookups is what assignment does, and the slide's example stores a phone number under a name.
Freed when Unit A retired its slide icons. This is the icon that opened the Naming section as a content slide, so it was already the author's pick for this exact concept.
Input in, work happens, output out.
The slide says "imagine a train pulling multiple cars" and shows a locomotive. Replaces layers, which read as depth rather than as a sequence.
Replaces `quotation`, which renders monochrome. A text object with handles, and it recolours.
A fixed, ordered set of levels.
A package with a plus on it. Replaces inbox-download, which read as a generic download rather than as adding a package.
A literal grid of rows and columns. The earlier pick was the abstract `data` glyph, chosen only because spreadsheet.json was in use on a Unit A content slide; retiring those icons freed the concept.
Looking at data before modelling it. PROPOSED: binoculars (dpmsxdtz). A magnifier reads as searching for something you already know is there; exploration is looking around before you know.
The apparatus of running a study. PROPOSED: clipboard-questionnaire (snlmykub).
The whole crowd, which is what a population is.
A tally counter: counting a subset by hand.
Aiming at a true value you cannot see.
A point estimate against an interval. PROPOSED: rulers, freed once C/07/a #4 takes tape-measure.
The library DOES have a bell curve, filed under `bitrate`. A curve over a histogram, which is the picture this section draws.
Many samples collapsing toward one shape. Check sales-leads-funnel against the bound funnel.json first.
A square stretching outward: a range rather than a point. The family has no error bar, and this is the nearest thing to one. PROPOSED: casino-chip (adaahleq).
The housekeeping at the end of the lecture.
A balance: H0 against H1, before any evidence.
The chain of reasoning, which is the section. PROPOSED: project-diagram (wsvtrygf).
Literal, and the title already invites it.

A cutoff being applied, and how blunt that is. PROPOSED: thumb-up (scjygvrg) with state=morph-down. Its morph runs up to down, so one icon enacts the verdict instead of depicting it. Supersedes both traffic-lights and chats-feedback: a traffic light has THREE states, which quietly endorses the marginally-significant reading this course argues against. CONFIRMED: use state=morph-down, so the thumb flips up to down.
Two variables related, which is all a correlation claims.
The arithmetic section.
Reasoning past the sample. Deliberately not magic_ball.json, which frames inference as fortune telling.
Two masks, which is a contrasting pair. Freed when Unit A retired its slide icons; it took avatars-woman-man's place when that went to dummy coding, where it is more specific.

Two arrows going opposite ways: two routes to the same comparison. Replaces two-way-traffic-sign, which suggested direction more than choice. PROPOSED: signpost-double (kjeyqivm). A signpost is a CHOICE between routes; two opposite arrows read as exchange or two-way traffic. signpost-right has only one arm. Adopting it frees arrows-left-right, which has no better home elsewhere and can sit in the catalog as a spare.
Measuring how big, not whether. The best fit in the catalog.
More than two groups at once.
The section where it becomes R. browser-code is taken by A/01/b.
Which pair differs, asked after the omnibus test.
The assumption failing, and the title's own metaphor.
The same people measured again.
The unit-closing activity is literally translation.

REPLACES the pilot's map.json, which is the roadmap slide's motif across six decks. SETTLED: keeps line-chart-markers. scatter-plot was proposed here but D/10/b #1 already has it and that lecture is entirely about reading scatter plots, so it keeps the claim. No export needed for this row.
Kept from the pilot.
REPLACES the pilot's location_pin.json: centering moves an origin, it is not a place.
Kept from the pilot. PROPOSED: tape-measure (wufezfky).
Predictors that are kinds rather than amounts. CLASH: puzzle-piece is already assigned to D/10/a #2. PROPOSED: radio_buttons, freed once C/07/b #3 takes card-suits.
The deck's own dichotomous example is penguins$sex with levels male and female, so the icon shows the variable being coded rather than a generic on/off.
Several levels, one reference. PROPOSED: card-suits (tpbwmgss).
Overlap is the whole idea.
Several predictors into one outcome. sitemap points the wrong way; check it renders as convergence. PROPOSED: diagram-venn (ohybxsin).
A bank of sliders: many inputs tuned at once.
A vista, for the overview of the moderation material.
Replaces `3-d`, whose colour slots are swapped so it renders green. Labelled X/Y/Z axes, which is the response surface itself.
Two arrows crossing: non-parallel slopes, drawn literally.
Re-centering with a product term in the model. Not crosshair: C/07/a has that and two would read as one.
Looking back at the previous lecture. review.json is taken.
One arrow up and one down: the two groups' slopes running opposite ways. Replaces sliders-vertical, which showed the continuous half and nothing binary.
Crossing arrows, a different variant from the arrows-crossed-right on C/08/a #3, so the moderation unit shares a family keyed to slopes that are not parallel.
A cell per combination of levels.
Three factors, three axes.
Straight lines stop being enough here.
The curved fit itself.
The library has no parabola. Both candidates are approximations of a single bend.
Blocks with a plus: another term added to the ones already in the model.
End of the section and of the unit.
The assumptions listed before any of them is checked.
The model's shape matching the data's shape.
A lost-and-found box: the cause that was there and never got measured.
A predictor that is the outcome again. Neither candidate is good; this one may be worth a wider search.
Two arrows running parallel the same way, which is what collinearity is: predictors saying the same thing. Replaces road-narrows-sign, which read as traffic.
Residual plots, which is what the whole lecture reads.
The fanning shape heteroscedasticity makes.

Checking a distribution rather than assuming one. PROPOSED: water-pipe (vnirazwq), played from `default:hover-pinch` so the leak shows. It sprays from the joint mid-animation and then seals. Residuals are what leaks out of the model, which is a better hook than a histogram, though the leak speaks to residuals in general rather than to their normality.
A family is a cluster of related observations, which is exactly what breaks independence. The icon draws the violation rather than the assumption.
The black sheep. One point unlike the rest.
